The Samajwadi Party will not come to power for the next 30 years, and the BJP will not go anywhere."

snippet.description:
Celebrate Halloween with these iconic Looney Tunes moments featuring Bugs Bunny, Witch Hazel, Porky Pig, Sylvester and Daffy Duck.

Episodes in order:
Transylvania 6-5000 (1963): While tunneling to Pittsburgh, Bugs Bunny mistakenly surfaces in Transylvania. He asks for directions at a mysterious castle, where he meets a vampire named Count Bloodcount. Now, with the count chasing him, Bugs finds a book with magic words that he uses against Bloodcount.

Hair-Raising Hare (1946): A mad scientist sends a sexy rabbit-robot to lure Bugs in as food for his monster. Bugs gets lured in by the robot and when he's face to face with the monster he freezes in a 'yipes!' position and then the long chase begins.

Broom-Stick Bunny (1956): Bugs makes a visit to Witch Hazel who is infatuated with her own ugliness and needs a rabit for her stew...

Claws for Alarm (1954): Porky and his pet, Sylvester, stay the night in a big, scary mansion.

Hyde and Hare (1955): Bugs gets himself adopted as a pet by a kindly soul who has been feeding him carrots every day. Bugs' friend turns out to be Dr. Jekyll who drinks his evil potion and turns into a monster. Bugs ended up drinking some of the potion and once back in the park he is transformed into a monstrous rabbit.

Bewitched Bunny (1954): Bugs enters the fairytale world to go save Hansel and Gretel from the witch.

A Witch's Tangled Hare (1959): In search of poetic inspiration, William Shakespeare comes across the castle of Macbeth and finds Witch Hazel chasing Bugs Bunny therein. The Bard jots down their dialogue as possibilities for dramatic situations.

snippet.title: why russia invaded ukraine
snippet.description:
Russia once gave Crimea away. So why did it invade Ukraine?

In 1954, Moscow handed Crimea to Soviet Ukraine. When the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, that line on the map became a border between two countries. This video traces how Crimea, the Donbas and the Black Sea coast came to be part of Ukraine, from Kyivan Rus to Catherine the Great, the Soviet era, the 1991 independence vote and the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, and sets out the reasons Russia's leaders give for the 2014 seizure of Crimea and the full invasion of 2022.

Russia's stated reasons are credited to the people who made them. Facts come from the sources below.

0:13 Kyiv and Rus
0:27 The Mongols, Lithuania and Moscow

1:05 The Donbas
1:16 Soviet Ukraine and the famine
1:28 The 1954 transfer of Crimea
1:45 Independence and the Budapest Memorandum
2:02 2014: Crimea and the Donbas

2:34 So why did Russia invade?

Sources:
